subject: Architecture
title: Space Stations: Architecture in Zero Gravity
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Space Stations: Architecture in Zero Gravity.

hook.text: The International Space Station is humanity's most extreme building — orbiting at 17,500 mph, 250 miles above Earth.

buildup.text: In zero gravity, there's no floor or ceiling — astronauts sleep on walls and work in any orientation.

discovery.text: Every surface must be functional — handholds, equipment mounts, and storage fill every inch of available space.

twist.text: Private companies are designing luxury space hotels — spinning to create artificial gravity for comfort.

climax.text: Axiom Space is building the first commercial space station module — attached to the ISS before going independent.

punchline.text: Architecture without gravity. Where up is wherever you want it to be.

quiz.question: How might future space hotels create artificial gravity?
options: By using magnetic floors that attract metal boots
By spinning the station to generate centrifugal force
By pumping heavy air that pushes occupants downward
